prompt:
Integrate the supplied OTP Input by TheShipar into my project. Treat the following three files as the exact source of truth for appearance, interaction, and animation. First inspect my framework and existing styles, then implement working files rather than only describing a solution. For a standalone demo, recreate these files verbatim in the same folder. For an existing app, adapt the mounting and asset paths to its conventions, scope demo styles so they do not affect unrelated pages, and preserve the reusable Web Component and its shadow-root styles. Do not add dependencies unless the host project requires them.


Preserve the compact 328px-wide six-digit input, 64px-tall rounded cells, centered layout, monochrome themes, restrained typography, label alignment during the merge, and subtle retry action. Preserve the 650ms merge, rolling blurred characters, asynchronous verification, left-to-right PASSED or RETRY! reveal, paste/autofill/keyboard behavior, screen-reader feedback, and reduced-motion support. Keep the theme toggle, attribution link, and demo instructions when recreating the demo; only include demo chrome in an existing app when appropriate.


The demo accepts any six digits except 000000, which triggers retry. This is a visual demo, not real authentication. For production, connect element.verify(code, { signal }) to the project's server verification endpoint and return true only on server-confirmed success. Never hardcode production OTP codes or secrets. Preserve reset and event APIs. The source-copy control itself is intentionally excluded from this three-file export; it is a distribution tool, not a dependency of the OTP component.

Now implement these files in my project using the requirements above. If no project is provided, deliver a runnable standalone folder containing the three files. If a project exists, integrate with its framework without changing unrelated features. Retain the provided visual proportions and motion rather than redesigning them. Verify numeric entry, paste, backspace, both themes, success, 000000 retry, reset, narrow screens, and reduced motion. Explain where the component was added, how to preview it, and where to attach real server verification. Clearly distinguish completed checks from anything you could not test.
